articles.title: Eat See Do: Hamburg
articles.description: “Hamburg, meine Perle” (Hamburg, my pearl) – few other songs have captured the love for this city as aptly as Lotto King Karl’s anthem. Germany’s second-largest city blends maritime grandeur with a sense of calm, perhaps because Hanseatic reserve and centuries-old merchant traditions still set the tone here today. As the country's largest seaport and gateway to the world, Hamburg has long been shaped by shipping, trade, and international influences – and the Hanseatic city remains every bit as cosmopolitan now as in the past. Even when the weather doesn’t cooperate, you can rely on the Speicherstadt, the harbor cranes, and that rugged North German elegance to retain their charm

Berlin has reinvented itself so often and recorded its history so visibly in the cityscape like few other cities in Europe. The fact that Berlin was at the center of the geopolitical conflicts of the 20th century can still be seen and experienced in many places, which gives the city a special historical depth. At the same time, Berlin snout, world-famous club culture, street art, creativity, and a strong inventive and innovative spirit characterize the attitude to life today

Sample world-class street food, discover Tel Aviv's Bauhaus architecture, or enjoy endless beach days on the city's 14-kilometer (9-mile) coastline. Find out everything you need to know to prepare for your trip here
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a coastal cityscape with modern buildings, palm trees, a lighthouse, and a sailboat on a beige background.

articles.title: Lufthansa in the Spotlight
articles.description: Gold records, Hollywood film shoots, famous passengers, and its own orchestra: the Lufthansa brand has been shaping pop culture for decades
articles.author: 100 years Lufthansa
articles.alternativeText: A concert in a glamorous theater hall with a band, orchestra, spotlights, and confetti

articles.title: Queer Travel: How to Make Your Vacation Safer and More Relaxed
articles.description: Queer people often prepare for trips differently. Not because they are more anxious, but because they have to consider things that never occur to many other travelers: can I hold hands with my partner? Do I have to hide my identity? Which dating app is safe? Lufthansa Insights has asked around in the community and compiled the most important tips for queer travelers
articles.author: Bo Kreter
articles.alternativeText: Two women wearing colorful shirts embrace and smile near tram tracks with a yellow tram in the background.

articles.title: A Perfect Day: Nice in One Day
articles.description: Discover Nice and the Côte d'Azur in just one day: Nihal, a personnel dispatcher at Lufthansa, reveals how travelers can experience the most beautiful and exciting places in the region even if they aren't staying long
articles.author: Nihal
articles.alternativeText: Aerial view of the crowded pebble beach and Promenade des Anglais along the sunny coast of Nice, France.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Tallinn
articles.description: We have put together three tips for an inspiring stay in Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. The city on the Baltic Sea inspires visitors with its unique mixture of medieval atmosphere and modern innovation. The historic old town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and transports visitors to another time with its winding streets and well-preserved buildings
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Historic colorful buildings with outdoor cafés and wooden planters in a sunlit European town square.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Zagreb
articles.description: Between magnificent façades from the Habsburg era, elegant parks, and a distinctive coffee house culture, Zagreb shows a Central European side of Croatia that surprises many. At the same time, the city exudes a relaxed, Southeast European joie de vivre that still characterizes squares, markets, and street cafés today. It is precisely this mix of elegance and serenity that makes Zagreb so special
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Panoramic view of the Zagreb cityscape with the Cathedral of the Assumption and historic rooftops under a blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Cagliari
articles.description: Cagliari is located on the south coast of Sardinia. The capital of the island is characterized by its proximity to the Mediterranean Sea and extensive history, which is tangible when strolling through the alleyways of the old town. If you are looking for authentic Italian life, you will find it in Cagliari, where the people are open and laid-back and very warm. Marvel at the flamingos that live in the city, admire the Roman amphitheater – or just let yourself drift and see what the day has in store
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Ancient stone tower on a rocky cliff overlooking calm sea during a golden sunset with mountains in the distance.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Almaty
articles.description: Nestled at the foot of the majestic Trans-Ili Alatau mountains lies Almaty, the former capital of Kazakhstan. Deeply rooted in the nomadic traditions of its inhabitants, Kazakhstan’s largest city offers a thriving culinary scene and a vibrant urban lifestyle. We’ll show you what makes this destination so surprising with its cultural contrasts against an alpine backdrop
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: A park in Almaty with a wide promenade, flower beds, and strollers, leading up to a pavilion-style viewing point on a hill against the striking backdrop of the Tian Shan mountains.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Vilnius
articles.description: Legend has it that a Grand Duke founded the city after hearing an iron wolf howl in a dream. The Lithuanian capital, situated on the banks of the Neris and Vilnia rivers, has retained the mythical spirit of its founding to this day. Discover an Old Town with Baroque splendor, the wonderful laid-back atmosphere of the Užupis artists' quarter, and much more
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Aerial view of the business district in Vilnius, featuring curved glass buildings, bridges, and a river, flanked by riverside paths and green spaces, with high-rise buildings in the background.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Casablanca
articles.description: The "White City" is a Moroccan port city and the largest metropolis in the country. Historically and architecturally, Casablanca was shaped by the French colonial period. Art Deco buildings and whitewashed façades characterize the cityscape. This mixture of Moroccan tradition and European influences also characterizes Casablanca in terms of its cuisine
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Ornate white church towers surrounded by green trees and palm trees under a clear blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Hyderabad
articles.description: A fascinating past as a center of the diamond trade and an equally impressive present as a thriving technology hub – southern India's Hyderabad embodies the interplay of tradition and modernity in a way that is almost emblematic of many cities across the subcontinent. Much of the cityscape is still defined by Indo-Islamic and Hindu architecture, while Hyderabad’s rich cultural heritage is also reflected in its distinctive culinary traditions
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Aerial view of a modern cable-stayed bridge over a lake in a bustling city with residential buildings and greenery.

articles.title: Eat See Do: St. Louis
articles.description: St. Louis still bears the nickname "Gateway to the West," a reference to the historical role of the city as a starting point for the expansion of the USA into the areas west of the Mississippi. The region is also known for its industrial history, blues, baseball, and special regional cuisine. Red brick façades, old warehouses, and the silver Gateway Arch characterize the look of the city
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Steamboat on the Mississippi River at sunset, with the Gateway Arch and the St. Louis skyline in the background.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Minneapolis–St. Paul
articles.description: Minneapolis and St. Paul are located on opposite sides of the Mississippi River as Twin Cities – to the west is modern, bustling Minneapolis with its skyline and lively music scene, and to the east is charming St. Paul with its Victorian villa districts. Learn more about what the Twin Cities have to offer here
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: View of the Minneapolis city skyline with the Stone Arch Bridge over the Mississippi River on a clear sunny day.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Riga
articles.description: With its 18th-century warehouses, restored Art Nouveau façades, and relics from the Soviet era, Latvia’s capital Riga tells the story of Europe in miniature. Anyone strolling through the historic Old Town and along the adjacent City Canal will find it difficult to escape the contrast between the museum-like cityscape and a youthful sense of new beginnings
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: House of the Blackheads on Town Hall Square in Riga

articles.title: Eat See Do: Algiers
articles.description: Algeria’s capital, Algiers, rightly bears the nickname "Alger la Blanche" (White Algiers): the city’s gleaming white buildings nestle against the slopes of the Sahel, a foothill of the Atlas Mountains, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Ottoman palaces, French colonial architecture, and vibrant North African modernism all shape the cityscape in equal measure. Here are our tips for a varied stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Square in Algiers with a fountain and palm trees in front of the white Moorish-style façade of the historic Grande Poste d’Alger.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Tirana
articles.description: The capital of Albania is now considered a real hidden gem. Located between the Adriatic coast and the mountains of Albania, Tirana combines Ottoman and socialist heritage, modern architecture, and urban lifestyle. Anyone who visits Tirana experiences this blend when eating, walking through the city, and on excursions. Find out here which culinary highlights should not be missed, which places are absolute must-sees, and which experiences make a visit to the capital special
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Skyline of Tirana with modern buildings, green parks, and mountains in the background under a clear blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Amman
articles.description: Amman is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world; the roots of the Jordanian capital can be traced back more than 3,000 years.  Ammman's bustling city center offers a charming contrast to its historic sights, with modern architecture, elegant hotels, art galleries, and boutiques
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Skyline of Amman, Jordan, showing modern high-rise buildings and dense residential areas under a clear blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Bogotá
articles.description: Bogotá is located where you would hardly expect a metropolis with millions of inhabitants: at an altitude of over 2,600 meters (8,660 feet), nestled in the eastern Andes Cordillera. Bogotá is raw and refined, colonial heritage and vibrant present all in one. From golden myths to colonial alleyways to Sunday streets filled with life – discover here what Bogotá has to offer
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Aerial view of a city skyline with tall buildings and green mountains under a cloudy sky.

articles.title: A Perfect Day: Nairobi in One Day
articles.description: Nairobi is a city of contrasts. You can be out in the wilderness just a few minutes away from the airport, complete with giraffes, lions, and zebras. This is what makes the Kenyan capital one of the world's most fascinating travel destinations for flight attendant Amrai-Careen Piephoh
articles.author: Amrai-Careen Piephoh
articles.alternativeText: View of the Nairobi skyline with City Hall in the foreground under a blue sky

articles.title: Eat See Do: Nairobi
articles.description: The Green City in the Sun, as Nairobi is known, is the only metropolis with a national park within its city limits. Nairobi also offers an exciting mix of traditional cuisine, diverse sights, and immersive experiences. Read on to find out what they are
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Three giraffes stand in the savanna with Nairobi’s skyline in the background, showing the close connection between wildlife and the city.

articles.title: In My Hood: Out and About in Karen and West Nairobi

articles.author: Christoph Eisenschink

articles.title: Eat See Do: Tbilisi
articles.description: A visit to the Georgian capital of Tbilisi should take in its fascinating history at the crossroads of east and west, the vibrant culinary culture, and the treasures in its many markets. Our recommendations lay out the culinary highlights that really capture the city’s flavors, the truly unmissable sights, and the experiences that will make a visit to this dynamic city on the Kura River live long in your memory
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Traditional wooden buildings with balconies in front of an ancient stone fortress on a sunny day.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Gothenburg
articles.description: The welcoming and pleasantly laid-back city of Gothenburg surprises visitors with its vibrant neighborhoods, top-class dining – including Michelin-starred restaurants – and a cultural scene that can hold its own against international cities. Find out here what you can experience in the "Amsterdam of Scandinavia"
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: A panoramic view of the Gothenburg skyline, featuring Oscar Fredriks Church and historic rooftops beneath a blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Ljubljana
articles.description: Here are our tips for an inspiring stay in Ljubljana, the charming capital of Slovenia. The "Green Capital of Europe" of 2016 captivates visitors with its car-free old town, the striking bridges designed by Jože Plečnik, and the imposing castle
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Bridge over the river with historic buildings and trees along the riverside on a sunny day in Ljubljana.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Thessaloniki
articles.description: Welcome to Thessaloniki, a vibrant city on the Thermaic Gulf in Greece. It is a treasure trove of history that invites you to explore its historic neighborhoods, but it also delights visitors with its diverse culinary scene along the waterfront. Discover all this and more with our tips for an unforgettable stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: White Tower of Thessaloniki near the waterfront promenade with tourist boats and cityscape in Greece.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Chennai
articles.description: For centuries, Chennai was one of the major port towns on the southeastern Coromandel coast and it is still considered the cultural center of South India today. Temple bells, jasmine blossoms at market stalls, and the honking of auto rickshaws are just as much a part of everyday life there as classical South Indian music and cricket on the beach. Our three tips showcase the culinary, sightseeing, and historical side to Chennai
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Hindu temple with ornate architecture, domes, and lush greenery under a clear blue sky.

articles.title: Eat See Do: Houston
articles.description: Houston is characterized by space exploration, the Wild West, and hearty BBQ culture. Yet this southern metropolis on the east coast of the USA also reveals a culturally diverse side. Here are our top three tips for an inspiring stay

Performing under the stage name Saucy Lady, she is a singer, recording artist, DJ, and music label owner who keeps dance floors moving with disco and '80s funk. articles.title: Know Before You Go: Casablanca
articles.description: Casablanca is the economic center of Morocco and at the same time the largest city in the country. Wide boulevards from the French colonial era, Art Deco buildings, and traditional markets define the cityscape as well as the hustle and bustle of life on the streets. We have summarized what you should know for a well-prepared stay in Casablanca here
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a Moroccan cityscape with traditional buildings, a mosque, tram, palm trees, boat, and cultural symbols.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Minneapolis–St. Paul
articles.description: Minneapolis was once the flour capital of the world, St. Paul the tranquil residence of the governor – and today the Twin Cities on the Mississippi together form a culturally dense and liveable metropolitan region. We have summarized the most important information for your stay so that you have more time for museums and spontaneous discoveries along the Mississippi
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a stylized city skyline with iconic buildings, a bridge, trees, and a river in blue, gray, and yellow tones.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Bogotá
articles.description: "La Atenas de Sudamérica" ("the Athens of South America") – that's what Colombians call their capital, and the nickname is justified. Bogotá has long been considered one of the most important centers for literature, education, and science in Latin America. It is a vibrant metropolis at an altitude of over 2,600 meters (8,660 feet), which can leave newcomers breathless at first – in the literal sense. Here's what you should know about the Colombian capital before your stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a city skyline with historic buildings, modern skyscrapers, mountains, palm trees, and a yellow bus.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: St. Louis
articles.description: The city of St. Louis was built where the Mississippi and Missouri Rivers meet, making it one of the main early transportation hubs in the US. To this day, industrial history, blues, baseball, and red brick districts characterize the cityscape – as does the Gateway Arch, a steel monument that towers over Downtown right on the riverbank. To help you find your way around St. Louis and make your stay as pleasant as possible, we have summarized the key information for you
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of St. Louis skyline with the Gateway Arch, Old Courthouse, stadium, a fountain, and a riverboat on a beige background.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Tbilisi
articles.description: Situated on the Kura River, Tbilisi is the rapidly modernizing capital of Georgia, offering visitors centuries of history and a distinctive food and wine culture. Read on for all the key information you need to plan your visit to this beautiful city at the crossroads of Europe and Asia
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a modern cityscape with diverse buildings, a bridge, and orange trees on a beige background.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Hyderabad
articles.description: The southern Indian city of Hyderabad combines centuries-old heritage with the pace of a modern tech metropolis. Here are our tips on transport, payments, tipping, and more to help travelers enjoy both sides of the “city of pearls”
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of Charminar monument with the cityscape and modern buildings in the background on a beige backdrop.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Tirana
articles.description: Tirana is the capital of Albania and is situated inland, right next to Dajti Mountain and around 40 kilometers (25 miles) from the Adriatic coast. The city has changed significantly over the course of its history, as evidenced by Ottoman influences, relics of its communist past, and modern, colorful façades. We have summarized what you need to know before your stay in Tirana
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: An illustration of a cityscape featuring a mosque, a clock tower, a modern skyline, mountains in the background, and a statue of a horseman in the foreground.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Almaty
articles.description: Along with the capital Astana, Almaty is still the cultural, scientific, and economic center of Kazakhstan – with universities, numerous sacred buildings, museums, and theaters. At the same time, the city is distinguished by its exceptional location: the mighty peaks of the Tian Shan Mountains rise right behind the city's skyscrapers. In addition, Almaty is considered one of the greenest cities in the former Soviet Union – characterized by parks, wide avenues, and numerous fountains. Here we have summarized what you should know about the Kazakh metropolis before your stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a cityscape featuring a mountain, TV tower, church, apple sculpture, and mountain goat statue.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Gothenburg
articles.description: The port city of Gothenburg on the western coast of Sweden is known for its enchanting archipelago islands, among other things. Plus, there's virtually no better place to enjoy high-quality, locally farmed seafood. We have summarized what you should know before your stay in Sweden's second-largest city
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a city skyline with a church, bridge, ferris wheel, cranes, buildings, and a ferry on water.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Thessaloniki
articles.description: Its rich history, lively waterfront, and vibrant café culture make Thessaloniki an enticing destination on the Greek Aegean coast. Here you’ll find all the information you need to plan a visit to this charming city
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of famous landmarks including castles, a domed building, sailboats, and a tower on a beige background.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Vilnius
articles.description: Vilnius is the capital of Lithuania and, with over 600,000 inhabitants, the largest city in the Baltic region. Here you’ll find Baroque churches, creative venues, and plenty of green spaces packed into a compact area. The city is easy to get to know, yet reveals many of its details only on second glance. We’ve summarized here what you should know before your stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: An illustration of a city skyline featuring several churches, cathedrals, a castle tower on a hill, and a television tower.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Chennai
articles.description: Chennai is located on the southeast coast of India and is considered the cultural center of the state of Tamil Nadu. Between grand colonial buildings, Hindu temples, miles of urban beaches, and one of the country’s most vibrant food scenes, a metropolis unfolds that is deeply shaped by tradition, film culture, and South Indian everyday life. Because Chennai is less touristy than other major Indian cities, it is worth getting to know key processes and routes in advance. Find out everything you need to know at a glance
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a coastal cityscape with a lighthouse, temple, church, clock tower, palm trees, and an auto rickshaw.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Algiers
articles.description: Algiers is considered the bright white pearl of the Mediterranean and fascinates visitors with the contrast of oriental and European influences. While the UNESCO World Heritage Site of the historic Kasbah boasts Ottoman palaces, magnificent French buildings, and the third-largest mosque in the world tower above the deep blue bay of the Mediterranean. We have summarized what you should know in advance about your stay in Algiers here
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a coastal cityscape with white buildings, boats, a mosque, towers, and palm trees in blue and yellow tones.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Amman
articles.description: The Jordanian capital of Amman combines rich history – it claims to be one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world – with a rapidly modernizing cityscape, spread across rolling hills and lively neighborhoods. Get your bearings with these tips for your visit to the “white city,” so called because of the light-colored buildings on the hills around this metropolis of the Middle East
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a modern train passing near historic buildings and an ancient amphitheater in a Middle Eastern cityscape.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Zagreb
articles.description: The Croatian capital, Zagreb, lies at the foot of the Medvednica mountain and is characterized by 18th- and 19th-century Austro-Hungarian architecture, as well as a remarkably high concentration of cultural attractions. The Upper Town grew out of two originally separate settlements and was complemented by a modern Lower Town, meaning that tradition and modernity meet head-on in Zagreb. We have summarized here what you should know before your stay in Croatia’s largest city
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: An illustration of a city scene featuring historic buildings, a church with twin towers, a statue of a horseman, a funicular railway, and a tram.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Berlin
articles.description: Berlin is the capital of Germany, and also the largest city in the country with almost 4 million inhabitants. It is an international metropolis where a diverse range of cultures, perspectives, and lifestyles meet. This diversity is evident in each neighborhood in its own way. We have summarized the most important information for your stay in the German capital here
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of Berlin landmarks including the Brandenburg Gate, TV Tower, Berlin Cathedral, Oberbaum Bridge, and Ampelmännchen symbol.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Beijing
articles.description: Beijing was laid out over the centuries along a clear north-south axis, which can still be seen today in the palace complexes, wide streets, and monumental squares. It is also a place where imperial history, socialist heritage, and modern city converge
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of iconic Chinese landmarks and cultural symbols including the Great Wall, Temple of Heaven, and a dragon.

articles.description: Ljubljana is one of the smaller capitals of Europe – and this is precisely what makes it so appealing. With around 300,000 inhabitants, the Slovenian capital is manageable, but at the same time surprisingly versatile: between a Baroque old town, a lively cultural scene, and lots of greenery, you'll discover a place that is quickly accessible to visitors – and on foot. Here we have summarized the most important information for a well-prepared stay
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team

articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a coastal fortress with towers, an elephant statue, palm trees, a boat, and flamingos in the water.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Nice
articles.description: Nice is the city on the Côte d'Azur where there's lots to see and do without having to go far: stroll through the old town in the morning, take a dip in the sea at noon, and visit a museum or the opera in the evening. Despite its Riviera flair, Nice remains an authentic city with markets, museums, and various districts, each with its own character. Because many things can be done in one day, it is worth getting the lay of the land before you go. We have put together a summary of what you should know in advance for your stay on the Côte d'Azur
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of a coastal cityscape with palm trees, historic buildings, a waterfall, tram, chairs, and a yacht.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Riga
articles.description: With its magnificent Art Nouveau buildings, a largely preserved or restored historic old town, bustling squares, and traditional markets, Riga exudes a unique form of urban elegance. The Latvian capital is compact enough for spontaneous exploration, yet so diverse that you can spend several days enjoying a variety of experiences. We have summarized here what you should know before your stay in the Latvian capital
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
articles.alternativeText: Illustration of the city of Riga, featuring historic buildings, a bridge, and a tram.

articles.title: Know Before You Go: Houston
articles.description: “Houston, we have a problem” is still considered one of the most famous phrases in the history of space exploration – even though the original transmission from Apollo 13 on April 13, 1970, was slightly different. The Texan metropolis remains closely tied to its role in space exploration, but it also boasts many other facets. We present the key information to help you plan a smooth trip
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team
